mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to potential monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher interest rates, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, positively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to potential economic slowdown, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy, which is generally positive for equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS < 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which can lead to increased consumer spending and economic growth, positively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 5% year-over-year, it signals strong consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS increases > 5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) both increase, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, which can negatively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase.
